title: Posteromedial Corner

positions.as_written: Examine the anterior cruciate in any knee with a corner injury, because the combination is commoner than either alone in this pattern.
Treat the corner as the extension restraint and the collateral ligament as the flexion restraint.
Assess the corner before any anterior cruciate reconstruction in a knee with medial findings.
Document valgus at 0 degrees, valgus at 20 degrees and rotation in extension separately, because the three together stage the injury and no one of them does.
Consider acute repair where the tissue is capsular and recently injured, since the blood supply supports it.
Avoid treating capsular tissue that has already stretched as repairable.
Plan the approach to expose more than the plan needs.
Repair and reconstruction answer different anatomies.
Consider the meniscus in every corner plan.
